title: A brief history of syslog timestamps, (Sun, Nov 22nd)
description: In early 2023, Debian 12 and Ubuntu 23.04 changed their default syslog timestamp format by dropping a configuration directive in the rsyslogd package. This change resulted in syslog timestamps switching from the traditional BSD format (Mmm dd hh:mm:ss) to ISO-8601 (RFC 3339) format. The change coincided with these distributions defaulting to systemd journal for logging instead of rsyslogd. Fedora and AlmaLinux retained the older configuration directive, preserving the traditional timestamp format when rsyslogd is installed. This change primarily affects system administrators who rely on rsyslogd for centralized logging and log forwarding.
